newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian survivors say fear more dead in shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: Albanian survivors say fear more dead in shipwreck.

text.p: Albanian refugees rescued after their boat capsized and sank in the southern Adriatic said on Saturday they feared many comrades had died in the accident.

Italian officials said four bodies of adults had been recovered and 34 people rescued when the boat with an unspecified number of people on board sank after being in collision with an Italian navy ship on Friday night.
Aircraft returned the area about 30 miles off southern Italy at first light on Saturday to resume a search for survivors.
Coastguard officials in Brindisi said they would be questioning the survivors individually to try to determine the exact number of people on board the boat at the time of the accident.

A defence ministry statement on Friday night said the small Albanian coastal patrol boat, with about 30 people visible on deck, collided with the corvette Sibilla which was trying to prevent it from entering Italian waters.
The defence minisry said: "The number of missing is for the moment unknown."

Survivors taken by the coastguard to the port of Brindisi port early on Saturday morning told reporters variously that there between 70 to more than 100 people on the ship at the time. A number of passengers were children, they said.
Police limited access to the survivors, with reporters and refugees shouting questions and replies in confusion on the dock.
"More than 50 of us died," an Albanian man shouted to reporters.
Survivors, many of them still wet, were examined at Brindisi dockside by doctors but there were no serious injuries that required hospitalisation, officials aid.
They were then taken by police by bus to an unknown destination in the southern port city.

More than 13,000 Albanians have reached Italy in the past two weeks on a flotilla of ancient and rusty boats after rebels in the impoverished Balkan country took control of towns in the south in an armed insurrection.
Italy, concerned that many refugees are simply looking for a better life abroad rather than fleeing real danger, has ordered its navy to patrol the Adriatic and advised Albanian boats to turn back.
The sinking was the first incident involving fatalities since the exodus of Albanians began on March 13.

The ministry statement on Friday night said the boat was first detected at around 1615 GMT off the southern Albanian port of Vlore and was approached by the navy ship Zeffiro which was under orders to prevent Albanians from illegally entering Italy.
"The ship ignored all calls from Zeffiro for it to halt, carrying out various evasive manoeuvres and continuing to head for Italy," it said.

"Later, the control of the Albanian ship was passed to the ship Sibilla, which at 1900 approached at slow speed. During this manouevre, the patrol boat carried out an abrupt shift to the right, cutting across the Sibilla's path.
"The Italian ship immediately stopped its engines and went into reverse but could not avoid the collision which caused the capsizing of the Albanian vessel."
A rescue operation was mounted, with personnel from both Italian ships, planes and helicopters later joined by coastguard vessels.

Italy has said it will grant temporary sanctuary to genuine refugees but will repatriate "undesirables". About 1,000 Albanians have been sent back, either for breaking the law since arriving in Italy or as suspected escaped convicts.
